newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian trade deficit widens, investment rises.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian trade deficit widens, investment rises.

text.p: Cambodia's trade deficit increased to 1.121 trillion riel ($407.6 million) in 1996, a rise of 38 percent over the previous year's deficit, the central bank said in a monthly report released on Friday.
But the National Bank of Cambodia also said net foreign direct investment was 575.9 billion riel ($209.4 million) in 1996, up nearly 30 percent from 1995.
The sectors which attracted most investment were banking, construction and light industry such as garments, tobacco, timber processing and beverage production, the bank said.

The bank said the trade deficit widened because of a sharp fall in re-exports. Discounting the decline in re-exports, Cambodia's domestic exports grew by 18 percent in 1996 compared with 1995, the bank said.
Total exports in 1996 declined by 424.6 billion riel ($154.4 million) while the value of imports fell by 118.2 billion riel ($43 million), the National Bank of Cambodia said.
The bank estimated that total exports last year were worth 1.7 trillion riel ($618.1 million), a fall of 20 percent from 1995.
The bank said that in addition to a fall in re-exports the trade deficit was affected by a 14 percent decrease in timber exports.
Cambodia is restricting most timber exports and attempting to enforce a logging ban following concern about illegal logging among foreign aid donors.
The bank said the garment sector grew strongly with exports worth 267.6 billion riel ($97.3 million) in 1996, or 35 percent of total domestic exports.
Cambodia's rubber industry, which analysts say is suffering from mismanagement and a lack of progress toward privatisation, continued to decline.
Rubber exports in 1996 were worth 83.9 billion riel ($30.5 million) compared with 101.1 billion riel (36.8 million) the previous year, the bank said. $1=2,750 riel
